question: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**esker**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel is known as an **esker**.
 
• Eskers are formed by the deposition of sediments from meltwater rivers flowing within and beneath glaciers.
 
• They are typically sinuous and can extend for several kilometers.
 
• Eskers are important geological features that help scientists understand past glacial processes and environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moraines** are accumulations of dirt and rocks that have fallen onto the glacier surface or have been pushed along by the glacier as it moves.
 
• **Erratics** are large boulders that have been transported and deposited by glacial ice, often found far from their source region.
 
• **Aquifers** are underground layers of water-bearing rock or materials through which groundwater can move.
 
• Understanding these geological terms is crucial for studies in glaciology, hydrology, and environmental science.
